brief.headline: Kopani and Ukrainske captured; Ukraine hits Crimea, fuel-strike campaign widens
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated claimed captures of Kopani (Zaporizhzhia) and Ukrainske (Kharkiv) alongside an escalating campaign against Ukrainian fuel infrastructure, while an unusually negative note ran through coverage of Ukrainian drone strikes on Crimea and Russian rear regions and persistent domestic fuel-shortage warnings.

developments.title: Claimed capture of Kopani in Zaporizhzhia widely reported
developments.body: Multiple channels claimed Russian marines liberated Kopani, reporting two Ukrainian platoons destroyed and a wedge forming toward Orekhovsk/Orekhov. Claims are channel-sourced and unconfirmed; the consistency across outlets suggests a coordinated messaging push.

developments.title: Ukrainske village claimed captured near Volchansk/Kupyansk
developments.body: Channels reported Russian forces took Ukrainske south of Volchansk on the Burluk direction, claiming a broken Ukrainian defensive line and expanded security zone. Unconfirmed and MoD-aligned framing.

developments.title: Fuel-infrastructure strike campaign framed as systematic
developments.body: Rybar claimed drones struck over 70 Ukrainian gas stations, mostly in Kharkiv, with further strikes reported across Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia. One blogger (Starshe Eddy) criticized strikes as too one-off, urging systematic destruction — a rare intra-camp critique. Claims unconfirmed.

developments.title: Ukrainian strikes hit Crimea energy and Russian regions
developments.body: Channels reported 300 Ukrainian drones launched overnight (179 claimed downed), power knocked out in Armyansk and Feodosia with rolling Crimean blackouts, and an OMON bomb-disposal officer killed in Kursk. This drove the day's negative sentiment spike on the topic.

developments.title: Konstantinovka: Ukrainian garrison abandoned, channels claim
developments.body: Arkhangel Spetsnaza claimed Ukraine's command deliberately abandoned the surrounded Konstantinovka garrison to hold Kramatorsk-Slavyansk, while Poddubny reported Russian mopping-up. Kotsnews noted Ukraine preparing Sloviansk/Kramatorsk for urban warfare. Unconfirmed.

developments.title: Domestic fuel shortage and infrastructure defense concerns
developments.body: Two Majors cited a Duma deputy saying fuel shortages persist until Trump-Putin agreements are implemented; NgP raZVedka echoed a realistic shortage outlook. Rybar called for restructuring air defense and protecting critical infrastructure — negative internal signals.

narrative_watch.title: Fuel war reframed as strategic logistics warfare
narrative_watch.body: Channels increasingly cast strikes on Ukrainian gas stations and refineries as a deliberate campaign to cripple military logistics, with one blogger demanding it be made more systematic.

narrative_watch.title: West portrayed as burdening citizens to fund rearmament
narrative_watch.body: Rybar frames UK's £15bn defense boost and German savings/pension shifts as leaders sacrificing domestic welfare for militarization.

narrative_watch.title: Negotiations quietly acknowledged as pragmatic necessity
narrative_watch.body: Rybar concedes negotiations are 'pragmatically necessary' given limited capacity to achieve full territorial objectives — a notably restrained note amid triumphalist frontline coverage.

mood_lines.text: Strongly positive (net +85); fuel-infrastructure campaign celebrated as widening and effective across multiple regions.
Upbeat (net +72) on claimed Kopani and Ukrainske captures and Konstantinovka advances; near-uniform triumphalism.
Sharply more negative (net -9, +62 move) after Crimea blackouts, Kursk casualty, and 300-drone overnight barrage claims.
Consistently hostile (net -79); UK/German rearmament and continued aid framed as reckless escalation.
Turned sharply negative (net -60, -80 move) on fuel shortages and rear-region drone vulnerability warnings.
Small volume, fully negative; sniping at MoD drone-reporting inconsistencies and mocking Ukrainian leadership travel.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine strikes on Russia mood drops 62 points
flag_texts.body: Sentiment on Ukrainian strikes fell to net -9 as channels reported Crimean power outages in Armyansk and Feodosia, an OMON officer killed in Kursk, and a claimed 300-drone overnight barrage.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal mood collapses 80 points
flag_texts.body: Coverage turned sharply negative (net -60) on persistent fuel-shortage warnings tied to Trump-Putin talks and infrastructure terrorism, plus Omsk warnings of insider drone attacks 2,500km from the front.

flag_texts.title: Watchlist topics silent
flag_texts.body: No posts on mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin; domestic grievances stayed focused on fuel supply and MoD reporting rather than leadership.
